page: OVHcloud c2-15 is a compute-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel processor based on the Haswell architecture, operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) with no hyperthreading, resulting in exactly one thread per core. Memory capacity is 15.0 GB, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate capabilities. The Passmark CPU score of 6764.0 and the Passmark CPU extended instructions test score of 5646.09 both rank in the average tier. However, raw computational throughput is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks placing in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks at 346.97 GB/sec but drops to a weaker tier for large uncached blocks, measuring 36.82 GB/sec for reads and 23.61 GB/sec for writes. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as Passmark encryption and single-threaded gzip compression, also fall into the lower 25% performance bracket.

For specialized workloads, the server achieves average performance on small-scale language models, processing 476.72 tokens per second for prompts and 103.75 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. Performance degrades significantly on larger models, with a 7B parameter model yielding poor results. Given the dedicated CPU cores and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level dedicated compute tasks, basic database operations, and lightweight web serving, though it is constrained by its older architecture and lower memory bandwidth on large datasets.
